parties.ourParty: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ("Company", the customer)
parties.counterparty: Hanover Direct, Inc. ("HDI", the site developer/host)

plans.note: Outline is partial (only sec-1.4, sec-5.4 surfaced), so scan the numbered articles between the preamble (sec-p0001) and the signature block (sec-p0072) for a 'Limitation of Liability'/'Liability' article. Check mutuality of any cap, whether it is tied to fees paid to HDI, and carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement and willful misconduct. If liability is disclaimed only in HDI's favour, that is a deviation.

Look for an 'Indemnification' article in the unenumerated body. HDI develops and hosts the site and handles Deerskin Products content, so we expect HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from the site platform and for its negligence/willful misconduct; confirm our reciprocal indemnity is limited to content/marks we supply. Flag as missing only if no indemnity language appears anywhere.

No covenant-not-to-compete heading is visible. Still scan the services/scope article and any 'Covenants' provision for restrictions on the Company selling Deerskin Products through other channels or building its own site; that phrasing often hides inside a scope or exclusivity paragraph rather than under a non-compete heading.

A site development and hosting deal commonly appoints HDI as sole/exclusive developer and host. Check the scope article and sec-1.4 (access rights) for 'exclusive', 'sole provider' or a prohibition on engaging other hosts; if present, confirm we retain the right to use other providers, or at least an exit and a term limit.

No pricing/MFN heading surfaced. Review the fees and payment article for any 'most favoured' or 'no less favourable terms' language; only a clause obliging the Company to give HDI its best terms is a deviation — an MFN running in our favour is welcome and should not be flagged.

sec-5.4 appoints representatives for each party, which is where a personnel non-solicit is often parked; check that section and the general provisions. If a non-solicit binds the Company, verify it is mutual, limited to ~12 months and carves out general advertising and unsolicited applicants.

The defined term 'Termination Date' confirms a termination article exists in the unenumerated body. Confirm the Company may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice without penalty or accelerated fees, and that HDI cannot terminate for convenience mid-term while we depend on the hosted site.

Check the term article associated with 'Termination Date' for auto-renewal. Assess renewal length, the non-renewal notice window (30–60 days preferred) and whether renewal pricing is capped; an uncapped uplift is noted in the rationale rather than treated as a standalone deviation.

Governing law sits in the miscellaneous article immediately preceding the signature block (sec-p0072). Both parties are US direct-marketing companies, so New York or Delaware is expected and acceptable; only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration would be a deviation.

Look in the general provisions near the end for 'Assignment'. Given HDI and the Company are affiliated direct-marketing entities, confirm we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without HDI consent, and that HDI has no termination right on our change of control.

sec-1.4 concerns HDI providing the Company access to systems/materials and is a likely home for ownership language; also scan for a dedicated 'Proprietary Rights' article. Confirm the Company owns the site deliverables it pays for, the Deerskin Products content, customer/order data and its marks, with no assignment of Company IP or data to HDI.

sec-1.4 grants the Company access to HDI systems/materials — review the grant's scope for affiliate and contractor use, whether it is stated as revocable at will, and whether it survives long enough to operate the site during the term.

No audit heading surfaced. Check the fees/records provisions for any HDI right to audit the Company's books or usage; if found, test for annual frequency, prior written notice, business hours, and HDI bearing its own cost. Records access running in our favour is a benefit and should not be flagged.

Scan the fees/termination articles for early-termination fees, stipulated damages or penalty interest payable by the Company. Service credits or performance remedies running to us are welcome and are not a deviation.

Look for a 'Warranties' or 'Representations' article and any all-caps disclaimer. We need HDI to warrant workmanlike development and hosting availability for a meaningful period with re-performance or fee refund as the remedy; a bare AS-IS disclaimer with no service warranty is a deviation.

No insurance heading is visible and inter-affiliate hosting agreements of this vintage often omit it. HDI hosts our site and handles order/customer data, so if no insurance article exists anywhere, treat as missing and request commercial general liability plus tech E&O/cyber cover with certificates.

Check the fees/compensation article for minimum monthly hosting fees, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay language binding the Company. Fixed recurring service fees alone are not a minimum commitment; only a guaranteed spend or volume floor without an exit is a deviation.

The 'Termination Date' definition points to a termination article — check it and the effects-of-termination paragraph for return of Company data, customer lists and site content, and for wind-down/migration assistance. If neither appears, record as missing and request data return in a usable format plus a defined transition period.
